outcome: experiences of child and adolescent eating disorder treatment
perceived helpfulness and acceptability of online treatment
cohort: The study included 90 participants (25 young people, 49 parents/caregivers, and 16 clinicians) involved in child and adolescent eating disorder treatment.
finding: Preferences for eating disorder treatment delivery are largely unchanged since 2020, with online treatment considered helpful and acceptable by all groups, but a strong preference exists for face-to-face early and final sessions, suggesting a hybrid and flexible model is optimal.
cross-section timing: Post-COVID-19 pandemic, with comparison to data collected in 2020 (earlier in the pandemic)
